facts.statement: Natunaornis gigoura was an extinct flightless pigeon that lived on Viti Levu, the largest island in Fiji.
facts.quote: The Viti Levu giant pigeon or Fiji giant ground pigeon (Natunaornis gigoura) is an extinct flightless pigeon of Viti Levu, the largest island in Fiji.

facts.statement: This species was only slightly smaller than the dodo and the Rodrigues solitaire.
facts.quote: It was only slightly smaller than the dodo (Raphus cucullatus) and Rodrigues solitaire (Pezophaps solitaria)

facts.statement: Remains were discovered in Quaternary cave deposits in October 1998 and November 1999.
facts.quote: Remains of this species were discovered in Quaternary (probably Holocene) cave deposits in October 1998 and November 1999.

facts.statement: The species was first described in 2001.
facts.quote: Its first description was published in 2001.

facts.statement: The holotype is held in the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa.
facts.quote: The holotype is in the collection of the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence includes a holotype tarsometatarsus and paratypes consisting of various wing and leg parts.
facts.quote: It is known from the holotype tarsometatarsus and paratypes including various parts of the wings and legs.

facts.statement: No skull parts are known except for a possible referred premaxilla.
facts.quote: No parts of the skull are known apart from a possible referred premaxilla (MNZ S37306).

facts.statement: The genus name honors Natuna, an elder of the Volivoli people in the Sigatoka Valley where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name "Natunaornis" is named after Natuna, the oldest chief of the Volivoli people in the Sigatoka Valley, wherein the fossil bones of the type species were first found.

facts.statement: The species name reflects its large size and proposed relationship to crowned pigeons of the genus Goura.
facts.quote: The specific name reflects both the large size of this fossil species and its proposed affinities to the crowned pigeons of genus Goura.

El género monotípico al que pertenece la especie, Natunaornis, fue nombrado en referencia a Natuna, el más antiguo jefe tribal del pueblo volivoli en el valle Sigatoka , en el que se hallaron los huesos de la especie tipo por primera vez.

facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)
